sections.content: You know *es decir* and *o sea* from B1 Unit 27, where you used them to say an idea again more simply. A reformulation marker says: "what comes next is the same idea, said another way." It does not add a new point; it makes the first one clearer, shorter or more exact. Two more markers do the same job: *en otras palabras* ("in other words") and *dicho de otro modo* ("put another way"). In all four, the new wording comes after the marker, and a comma (or a semicolon in a longer sentence) separates it from what came before.

sections.title: Four ways to restate
rows: El viaje es largo; es decir, dura más de diez horas.
The journey is long; that is, it takes more than ten hours.
Salgo temprano, o sea, a las seis de la mañana.
I leave early, I mean at six in the morning.
La reunión es opcional; en otras palabras, nadie tiene que ir.
The meeting is optional; in other words, nobody has to go.
Hoy no hay clase; dicho de otro modo, tenemos el día libre.
There is no class today; put another way, we have the day off.

sections.content: Choose by tone. *O sea* is the most spoken; *es decir* works in talk and in writing; *en otras palabras* and *dicho de otro modo* suit a talk or text that has just said something abstract or long. You know *además* from A2 Unit 28: use that, not these four, when the second part adds a new fact.
